newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybean ends mixed on uncertainty.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybean ends mixed on uncertainty.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mixed on Friday on an uncertain short-term market trend, with the January contract supported by speculative buying, traders said.
The key January 1997 contract ended at an intra-day high of 3,230 yuan ($389) per tonne, up five yuan. It opened at a low of 3,200.
March fell 40 to 3,198, May rose 100 to 3,380, July put on 10 to 3,360, September fell 30 to 3,350 and November fell 10 to 3,380. Combined volume rose to 10,900 tonnes from 8,600.
Traders said investors remained on the sidelines due to a lack of market-moving news.

"The outlook for soybean futures in the short term is not clear and retail investors dominated today's trade," one trader said. "The spot price of 3,200 yuan per tonne has supported the January contract lately."
Traders expect soybeans to continue moving in a narrow range in the next few days.
